system.name: COMPAS
system.one_liner: an architecture for multivariate trace estimation across networked quantum processors via a distributed multi-party SWAP test

content.subject: how four multi-party SWAP-test circuit variants trade off GHZ width against circuit depth

elements.name: GHZ-⌈k/2⌉
elements.role: prepares a ⌈k/2⌉-qubit GHZ state that serves as control qubits for the SWAP test

elements.name: ρ1–ρ8
elements.role: eight data qubits (one-qubit states) permuted by controlled-SWAP gates

elements.name: × (SWAP)
elements.role: controlled-SWAP gate between two data qubits, controlled by one GHZ qubit

elements.name: H
elements.role: Hadamard gate applied to each GHZ control qubit before it is measured

elements.name: measurement gauge
elements.role: measures each GHZ control qubit in the X or Y basis to yield the SWAP-test outcome

relations.what: each GHZ qubit controls two rounds of SWAPs between the data qubits
after both SWAP rounds the GHZ qubits proceed to the Hadamard gate
each GHZ qubit is measured to extract the SWAP-test estimate

panels.label: (a) 1-qubit states
panels.differs: baseline scheme for one-qubit states: GHZ width ⌈k/2⌉, depth 2

panels.label: (b) deeper circuit
panels.differs: generalizes to n-qubit states by repeating the SWAP rounds n times, keeping GHZ width ⌈k/2⌉ but growing depth to 2n

panels.label: (c) wider GHZ
panels.differs: generalizes to n-qubit states by widening the GHZ state to ⌈k/2⌉n qubits, keeping depth at 2

panels.label: (d) parallel Toffoli via Fanout
panels.differs: replaces the SWAP rounds with a parallel-Toffoli block built from Fanout gates, keeping GHZ width ⌈k/2⌉ and depth O(1)
panels.verdict: ours, optimal in both depth and width

content.key_idea: Four circuit designs for the multi-party SWAP test trade GHZ-state width against circuit depth when scaling to n-qubit states; the paper's scheme (d) uses parallel Toffoli-via-Fanout gates to get both optimal depth and width.
content.reading_order: Left to right within each panel along the qubit wires from GHZ preparation to measurement; the four dashed panels are compared left to right as (a) through (d).

evidence: Unlike other schemes, which must choose between asymptotic optimality in circuit depth or GHZ width, COMPAS achieves both at once.
using a deeper circuit or increasing the width of the GHZ state

summary: This figure from the COMPAS paper compares four circuit implementations of the multi-party SWAP test, the subroutine COMPAS distributes across networked quantum processors. Each of the four dashed panels follows the same template: a GHZ-state preparation box supplies control qubits for two rounds of controlled-SWAP gates over data qubits labelled rho_1 through rho_8, followed by Hadamard gates and basis measurement. Panel (a) is the baseline one-qubit-state scheme, with GHZ width ceil(k/2) and depth 2. Panels (b) and (c) generalize to n-qubit states by either repeating the SWAP rounds n times, growing depth to 2n, or widening the GHZ state by a factor of n, with the added n term highlighted in red. Panel (d), COMPAS's own scheme, replaces the SWAP rounds with parallel Toffoli gates via Fanout, drawn as a single pink block, achieving constant O(1) depth while keeping the GHZ width at ceil(k/2).
summary_zh: 该图比较COMPAS论文中多方SWAP测试的四种电路：(a)单比特基线；(b)(c)加深电路或加宽GHZ态推广到n比特，红色标出新增n因子；(d)为本文方案，用Fanout并行Toffoli门（粉色）同时达到O(1)深度和最优GHZ宽度。
